title: Spring Boot
blurb: The full Spring Boot ecosystem, module by module, plus interview Q&A.

quiz.question: What does @SpringBootApplication combine?
quiz.explanation: It's a meta-annotation for @SpringBootConfiguration (a @Configuration), @EnableAutoConfiguration and @ComponentScan of the class's package and sub-packages.

quiz.question: Why does calling a @Transactional method from another method in the same bean often not start a transaction?
quiz.explanation: Spring applies @Transactional through a proxy; this.method() calls the target directly, skipping the proxy. Move the method to another bean or restructure the call.

quiz.question: By default, @Transactional rolls back on…
quiz.explanation: The default rollback rule is unchecked exceptions (RuntimeException) and Errors; checked exceptions commit unless you add rollbackFor.

quiz.question: Which injection style is recommended for required dependencies?
quiz.explanation: Constructor injection allows final fields, fails fast when a dependency is missing, and makes classes trivial to unit test with plain new.

quiz.question: In Spring Boot 4 / Spring Framework 7, what is the recommended synchronous HTTP client?
quiz.explanation: RestClient is the fluent synchronous client; the Spring team plans to deprecate RestTemplate in Framework 7.1 and remove it in 8. WebClient remains the reactive option.

problems.title: Find the N+1
problems.prompt: GET /customers returns 50 customers and logs 51 SQL queries because each CustomerDto reads customer.getOrders(). Give two fixes.
problems.solution: Load the association in the same query: a repository method with @Query("select distinct c from Customer c left join fetch c.orders") or @EntityGraph(attributePaths = "orders"); or skip entities and select a DTO projection with only the needed columns. Paginating with a collection fetch join needs care (fetch IDs first, then fetch join by IDs). Verify with SQL logging or Hibernate statistics.

problems.title: Health probes on Kubernetes
problems.prompt: Configure a Spring Boot service so Kubernetes stops sending traffic while it's warming up, but doesn't restart it.
problems.solution: Enable management.endpoint.health.probes.enabled=true (on by default when Boot detects Kubernetes) and point the readinessProbe at /actuator/health/readiness and the livenessProbe at /actuator/health/liveness. Readiness failing removes the pod from Service endpoints; only liveness failing triggers a restart. Add a startupProbe for slow starts.
